text: رَفِيق. In Arabic, it means companion.
That's what this app was made to be: a companion for anyone studying Arabic.
In a class, at a madrasa, or on your own, lessons give you new words. Keeping them is the hard part.
So everything here is built on what memory research says works.
Spacing. Coming back to a word after a gap beats cramming. It's one of the most replicated findings in memory research.
Testing. Pulling a word from memory strengthens it more than reading it again.
Habit. A little every day. In one well-known study, a daily habit took about sixty-six days to feel automatic.
So رَفِيق brings each word back just before you'd forget it, and asks you to recall it, not just reread it.
Use it to revise alongside your course. Or start from nothing at all.
Can't read Arabic yet? Begin with the twenty-eight letters, in families that share a shape.
Every letter comes with three words, the letter in red, and a native voice to copy.
Then the vowel marks, and a listening test to train your ear.
From your first letter to your first conversation.
A few minutes a day, with a companion beside you.
